text:
customer_acme: Hey team — we pinned a model for a customer env last night and now their embeddings are the wrong length. They used to get 1536 floats, now the array length is 1024. This broke our indexer. We pin with model=pinned-acct-42 via the API. Any idea?

emily_support: Thanks for the report — sorry about the hit. Can you paste the exact request you used (no creds) and one full embedding response (or just the length)? Also which account/org id and when you did the pin?

customer_acme: We pinned around 2024-11-22 03:12 UTC. Here's a redacted curl we used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ***' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"pinned-acct-42","input":["hello world"]}'
```
Response snippet: "embedding": [0.00123, 0.00234, ...] length = 1024. Previously it was 1536 for the same dataset.

emily_support: Ok — two likely causes: 1) the pinned alias was pointed to a different model variant with 1024-dim outputs, or 2) a post-processing step (client-side) is truncating vectors. Can you run this quick python check on a single item?
```python
from requests import post
resp = post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={'model':'pinned-acct-42','input':'test'})
print(resp.json())
print(len(resp.json()['data'][0]['embedding']))
```
This will confirm server-side.

customer_acme: Ran it — confirmed: server returns 1024 length. We did not change client trimming.

raj_infra: I can check alias mappings and the rollout logs. On it.

deploy-bot: [deploy] alias-update service:alias reconciler ran for account=pinned-acct-42 at 2024-11-22T03:09:12Z, action=apply, note="map alias to model open-embed-1b-quant@v1.3"

raj_infra: Ok I pulled the alias history: pinned-acct-42 was originally mapped to `open-embed-2b@v2.0` (1536 dim). At 2024-11-22T03:09 we applied a batch alias reconciliation job that accidentally pointed a subset of pinned aliases to the lower-cost quantized variant `open-embed-1b-quant@v1.3` which outputs 1024 dims. The reconciliation script used a cost-savings list and `pinned-acct-42` was included by mistake.

emily_support: That matches symptoms. Do we have audit logs / who triggered reconciliation?

raj_infra: The batch job is automated by cost-ops; reconciler ran as part of a rolling cleanup against stale alias entries. Logs show rule `reduce-cost-nonprod` matched the alias because the account label was `env:staging` — customer had staging tag on the alias. I see commit id and job id: job-20241122-0309. I will snapshot the mapping and prepare rollback.

maria_product: This is a policy bug — pinning should be honored regardless of cost reconciliation. We need a hard guard: if alias.isPinned==true, skip cost reconciliation. Also notify affected customers.

tim_engineer: For immediate mitigation I can re-point the alias back to the original model. Command I will run (internal):
```
redwoodctl alias update --alias pinned-acct-42 --model open-embed-2b@v2.0 --by tim_engineer --reason "rollback wrong reconcile"
```
I will also add an assertion that model.vector_size == expected_vector_size when updating alias.

raj_infra: Rolled back mapping at 2024-11-22T04:05Z. Current alias -> `open-embed-2b@v2.0`. Verified by calling the embeddings endpoint for the alias; now response length is 1536.

emily_support: Great. customer_acme, can you confirm your clients are now seeing 1536 vectors? If you cached any embeddings from yesterday you'll need to reindex or run a migration script (we can help).

customer_acme: Confirmed — production indexer starts to see 1536 again for new requests. We do have ~24k vectors stored with 1024 length from the window. We'll need a migration plan.

maria_product: We'll follow up with an incident email and a postmortem. Immediate action items: 1) roll out a guard in reconciler (skip pinned aliases), 2) add verification step to alias updates that checks vector dimension, 3) notify customers with pinned aliases that were affected and offer one-time credits for reindexing, 4) add monitoring alert for sudden per-account embedding_dim changes.

tim_engineer: Quick repro steps I used for local testing (so SREs can validate):
1) create alias `alias-test-dim` -> `open-embed-2b@v2.0`
2) call embeddings -> assert len == 1536
3) run reconciler with patch that maps alias -> `open-embed-1b-quant@v1.3`
4) call embeddings -> assert len == 1024
5) rollback alias and assert len == 1536

Code snippet to verify vector dims in bulk (python):
```python
import requests
inputs = ['a','b','c']
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings', json={'model':'alias-test-dim','input':inputs}).json()
shapes = [len(x['embedding']) for x in resp['data']]
assert all(s==shapes[0] for s in shapes), shapes
print('dim', shapes[0])
```
This also catches cases where batched requests include mixed outputs (shouldn't happen).

emily_support: Ops note: customers can temporarily pin to an explicit model id (open-embed-2b@v2.0) instead of alias to bypass reconciler until guard is in prod. But we should not recommend that as long-term because it bypasses normal model upgrades.

raj_infra: Root cause summary for the ticket: automated alias reconciler matched pinned aliases with a 'staging' label due to an earlier tagging mistake and remapped them to a lower-dimension quantized variant. Fixes deployed: reconciler skip rule for pinned=true; alias-update validation; alerting for embedding_dim delta > 10% per-account.

maria_product: Marking as high priority postmortem. We'll draft comms and a one-time credit offer for affected customers. Also adding an SDK check that raises a warning if client sees an unexpected dim change vs recorded expected dim (helpful for quicker detection).

customer_acme: Appreciate the quick turnaround. Could you also provide a short script to detect mismatched dims in our index and generate reindex candidates? That would help.

emily_support: Yes — we'll share a utility script and propose credits. I'll follow up in a support ticket with next steps and the migration script attachments. :thumbsup:
